claims.text: Standard additive manufacturing of cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi produces compositional gradients, residual-stress accumulation, and microstructural defects.
An in-situ laser-remelting step immediately after each deposited layer will improve the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
In-situ laser remelting will reduce compositional segregation in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
In-situ laser remelting will reduce residual thermal stress in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
In-situ laser remelting will reduce processing-induced defects in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Real-time thermal and melt-pool monitoring can ensure optimal remelting energy delivery.
The intervention will produce a more uniform microstructure by reducing compositional gradients and defect density.
Rapid targeted remelting of each fresh layer permits thermal homogenization.
Moderating cooling rates through controlled resolidification minimizes segregation.
Thermal homogenization during remelting relieves residual stress.
Reducing defects through controlled laser processing enhances mechanical performance.
Remelted samples will exhibit at least a 10–20% improvement in both mechanical strength and ductility relative to AlCrFeNiSi made by additive manufacturing without remelting.
Remelted samples will have lower residual stress and less microsegregation than samples made without remelting.
The intervention is valid for laser-based additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi and for tensile and fatigue evaluation at ambient and moderately elevated temperatures.
The magnitude of improvement will depend on laser-parameter tuning and the thermal cycle.
